text:
elena: spotted something odd in partner-sink logs — looks like a raw Vault ciphertext ID leaked in an HTTP payload to partner's endpoint. payload contains `vault://transit:cty-0x7f4b...`. Not plaintext creds but still sensitive. Opening incident.

joel: Good catch. If it's just ciphertext we still need to treat as high because partner might have keys. Steps: 1) rotate transit wrapping key, 2) revoke any derived decrypt grants, 3) rotate any Vault tokens that could decrypt.

sec-oncall: Triage started. Querying Vault audit to see which principals accessed transit/decrypt for that key in the last 30d. Running: `vault audit search --path transit/rewrap-key --op decrypt --since 30d`

vault-bot: Audit event: principal=ci-runner@redwood used transit/decrypt on rewrap-key@v1 at 2026-03-21T19:12:04Z

ana: (ana) I can take wrap-key rotation. Plan: create new cryptoKey in KMS (ephemeral-wrap-v2), rewrap ciphertexts via KMS rewrap API, then update Vault transit to point to new wrapping-key version. Will need list of ciphertext identifiers to rewrap.

elena: I pulled the payload sample and added it to the private incident bundle: `cty-0x7f4b56...` (redacted). Also seeing identical pattern in 3 other partner requests from past 48h — adding those samples.

joel: I'll push an immediate RBAC restriction: remove transit/decrypt from CI service account and apply temporary policy `deny-transit-decrypt` for all non-oncall principals. Executing now.

infra-automation: IAM change applied: removed role "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter" from ci-runner-sa for keyRing ephemeral-ring. Change-id: change-20260323-01. Also added org-policy to block KEY_CREATE for infra projects until followup.

sec-oncall: Audit results: 4 decrypt ops between 2026-03-02 and 2026-03-21 by ci-runner@redwood. No external principals found. Exporting full audit to /secure/incidents/4988888888/audit.csv and notify SRE and Legal.

ana: Rewrap plan executed: used KMS `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/ephemeral-ring/cryptoKeys/ephemeral-wrap-v2` and ran `gcloud kms keys versions add` then `gcloud kms rewrap --ciphertext=cty-0x7f4b56... --destination-key=ephemeral-wrap-v2`. Verified decrypt with new key in staging.

elena: After rewrap, updated Vault transit config: `vault write sys/wrapping-keys/rewrap-key config=ephemeral-wrap-v2@v2` and restarted vault-agent for infra namespace. Tests show decrypt/encrypt succeed.

joel: Also pushed RBAC policy to Vault: removed `transit/decrypt` from `ci-runner` Vault token role and tightened TTL to 10m for CI runners. Policy id: vault-pol-20260323-01.

partner-monitor: Reached out to partner security contact (sec@partner.example). Partner says they don't persist KMS keys and confirm they didn't attempt decrypt. They rotated their own ingestion tokens as precaution.

sec-oncall: Running a wider scan: grepping partner logs back 14d for patterns like `vault://transit:`. Found 7 additional occurrences across `partner-sink` and `legacy-sftp-bridge`. Marking legacy-sftp-bridge as higher risk since it lacks workload identity.

ana: For legacy-sftp-bridge we should schedule a rotation sweep of associated service account keys and move to workload identity. I'll draft migration playbook and timeframe.

elena: Immediate action items: 
- ana: finish rewrap and post KMS rewrap audit evidence (command outputs) 9owner
- joel: confirm IAM/Vault deny policies and paste diffs 9owner
- sec-oncall: export audit csv + notify infra leads and legal 9owner
- infra-automation: create INFRA-4099 to scan partner logs org-wide and automation to detect `vault://transit` patterns 9owner
Timeline: containment actions done now, migration of legacy bridge in next 48h, postmortem at 21:30 UTC.

infra-automation: Created INFRA-4099: "org scan for leaked vault transit identifiers + automation". Linked artifacts: /secure/incidents/4988888888/* and policy change-id.

joel: Pasted outputs: `gcloud kms rewrap --ciphertext=cty-0x7f4b56... -> OK`, `vault policy write vault-pol-20260323-01 -> OK`, `gcloud iam remove-iam-policy-binding -> OK`.

ana: Rewrap evidence uploaded to incident bundle. Also rotated wrapping key version to v3 and updated Vault transit alias. Decryption tests passed.

sec-oncall: Confirming audit: no external principals decrypted the affected ciphertexts. All access from internal CI tokens that are now denied. Closing containment. Follow-ups: rotate SA keys for legacy-sftp-bridge, migrate bridge to workload identity, add log scanner to infra pipeline, and update runbook to treat any `vault://transit` leakage as high-sev.

elena: Thanks everyone. I'll own the rotation sweep across similar connectors and will post a status update to #eng-security-private once complete. Postmortem scheduled 21:30 UTC.
